title: Expose all Streamlit Types, I.E UploadedFile from file_uploader input
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Title is straight forward, in terms of trying to make a very type safe python application, having access to the types used from a library is paramount, so wondering why these types are not accessible as an import from the lib.

comments.body:
**To help Streamlit prioritize this feature, react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-7801)

Yeah good point, we should do that. We probably need to find a good place where we expose classes like this. I think we thought about having an `st.typing` namespace at some point. Anyway, will prioritize this when it gets more upvotes!

[USER]  I've also had to import this UploadedFile type from deeper in the streamlit API than I care to for my own application. An `import streamlit.typing as stt` (where typing.pyi is just a stubs module, if you don't want to provide user access to the actual classes themselves) would be super useful; it could contain things like `StreamlitAPIException`, `UploadedFile`, `DeltaGenerator`, etc...
[USER] [USER] I also had to import the UploadedFile type in an inconvenient manner. Providing library types for end users is quickly becoming standard practice.
[USER] Let me know if you disagree with any of the initial additions here; I think it's a reasonable place to start (small).
Great job [USER], when do we think the types module be ship to production?
I think that depends on the maintainers ([USER], for example). I am currently working on GH-8112 though.

We don't have a concrete plan to work on this right now unfortunately. Would one of you be interested in working on a PR at some point? I'll bring it up with the team for discussion but I think at least exposing the basic types like `UploadedFile` in a separate namespace shouldn't be a controversial topic.

# Proposed solution

- Add a new module `streamlit.typing` (this is similar to what e.g. NumPy does, they have `numpy.typing`).
- This module should definitely contain `UploadedFile`. I couldn’t find anything else that should obviously be in there but might make sense to have another look through the library.
- What this should **not** contain:
    - `DeltaGenerator` → not clear if we want to keep this long-term, and there are no requests for it at the moment
    - Exceptions → these are already in `streamlit.errors`
- I think the `streamlit.typing` module should also be mentioned in the docs. We can start very small though and just use the existing docstrings for types (e.g. see [[here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/c16232e330f084a9575ad54ab2dc78d6368df60c/lib/streamlit/runtime/uploaded_file_manager.py#L58)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/c16232e330f084a9575ad54ab2dc78d6368df60c/lib/streamlit/runtime/uploaded_file_manager.py#L58) for UploadedFile).

## Update 

Streamlit 1.62+ will expose various types/classes as part of the `streamlit.typing` namespace (also available as `st.typing`).
